nodes.name: Galvanic Replacement
nodes.procedure: The Ru-Ni(OH)2 catalyst was directly constructed on the surface of a hierarchical nanoporous nickel foam (NF) using classic galvanic replacement via spontaneous redox reaction between Ru3+ and Ni surface in N2 purged aqueous condition, where Ru3+ is reduced to Ru0 and Ni0 is oxidized to Ni(OH)2 on the surface of NF.

unit_operations.name: Galvanic Replacement
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: galvanic replacement between RuCl3 and metallic NF in an N2 purged aqueous condition

nodes.source_text: Figure 1a: Schematic illustration of the galvanic replacement between RuCl3 and metallic NF in an N2 purged aqueous condition... The microscopic redox reaction mechanism between the Ru3+ and Ni surface was simulated... suggesting a spontaneous and rapid process of Ru3+ reduction into Ru0 and Ni0 oxidation into Ni(OH)2 on the surface of the NF.

nodes.description: OER performance in O2-saturated 1.0 M KOH (three-electrode)
nodes.source_text: The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity of Ru - Ni(OH)2 was evaluated in O2 -saturated 1.0 M aq. KOH solution... iR-compensated polarization curves (Figure 3a; Figure S13, Supporting Information) suggested the Ru - Ni(OH)2 required an overpotential of 228 mV to reach a current density of 10 mA cm-2 ; ... Ru - Ni(OH)2 showed the smallest potential gap of 182 mV between 10 and 1500 mA cm-2

It required an overpotential as low as ∼ 15 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm-2 ... high current density of 1500 mA cm-2 (OER: 410 mV ; HER: 240 mV) ... low Tafel slope of ≈ 34 mV dec-1 ... Ru - Ni(OH)2 displayed a high TOF value of 1.51 s-1 at an overpotential of 25 mV

nodes.description: AEMWE bifunctional performance at different temperatures
nodes.source_text: The Ru - Ni(OH)2 / NF -based zero-gap MEA was first investigated in 1.0 m aq. KOH solution from 20°C to 80°C (Figure 5b); it required the cell voltages of 1.51, 1.57, 1.63, and 1.73 V at 20°C, 40°C, 60°C, and 80°C, respectively, to reach a current density of 150 mA cm-2 . The AEMWE with the Ru - Ni(OH)2 could reach a high current density of 350 mA cm-2 at an applied cell voltage of only 1.71 V

nodes.source_text: The accelerated degradation test also confirms the electrochemical stability of Ru - Ni(OH)2 in Figure 3g; the current density is saturated at 90.2% of the initial value
Long-term chronopotentiometry testing verified the structural integrity of the Ru - Ni(OH)2 during HER (Figure S24, Supporting Information)

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show controlled growth of thin Ru-Ni(OH)2 nanosheets over various Ru salt concentrations.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images in Figure 1c-h; Figure S2, Supporting Information show the controlled growth of Ru - N_i(OH)_2 over various Ru salt concentrations.

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM image shows Ru NPs with hexagonal lattice pattern and lattice fringe distances of 0.234 nm and 0.206 nm assignable to (110) and (101) crystalline planes of metallic Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ru NPs with a hexagonal lattice pattern were clearly spotted and are marked in the figure by a blue dashed circle. The lattice fringe distances of 0.234 and 0.206 nm were assignable to the (110) and (101) crystalline planes of metallic Ru.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM confirms abundant Ru NPs over sheet-like Ni(OH)2 with average size distribution of ≈8 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field-scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) image at bright field confirms the abundant existence of Ru NPs over the sheet-like Ni(OH)2 (Figure 1j) and their average size distribution of ≈8 nm (Figure S4, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru content within Ru-Ni(OH)2 detected as 5.55 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ru content within Ru - Ni(OH)_2 was detected to be 5.55 wt% from inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) measurements.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping shows Ru-Ni(OH)2 catalyst mainly consists of O, Ni, and Ru elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Further elemental mapping images suggest the Ru - Ni(OH)_2 catalyst mainly consisted of oxygen (O), Ni, and Ru elements (Figure 1k).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru 3p XPS shows peaks at 486.1 and 464.2 eV for Ru-O bonds indicating unsaturated Ru^{x+} sites; Ni 2p shows 0.25 eV negative shift compared to Ni(OH)2 reference.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2a compares the Ru 3p X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) spectra of Ru - Ni(OH)_2 and metallic Ru (Ru^0). Doublet peaks centered at ≈483.7 and 461.7 eV could be indexed to the Ru 3p_{1/2} and Ru 3p_{3/2} of metallic Ru, respectively. Two other peaks with binding energies of 486.1 and 464.2 eV were ascribed to the formation of Ru - O bonds...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES confirms oxidized valence state of Ru NPs (≈0.7); Ni K-edge XANES shows small pre-edge peak at 8333 eV indicating distorted Ni coordination environment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The normalized X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectra (Figure 2c) at the Ru K-edge confirmed the 4d electron density change and unbalanced charge state of the Ru NPs in Ru - Ni(OH)_2. The Ni K-edge XANES spectra (Figure 2e) of the Ru - N_i(OH)_2 sample exhibited a small pre-edge peak at 8333 eV...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge EXAFS shows Ru-O-Ni coordination at ≈1.59 Å and reduced coordination numbers of Ru-Ru (≈1.25) and Ru-O (0.32); Ni K-edge shows local atomic environment identical to Ni(OH)2 reference.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transforms of extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra and Wavelet transform (WT) analysis show two peaks at ≈1.54 and ≈2.33 Å for Ru acetylacetonate and Ru foil, respectively... For Ru - Ni(OH)_2, the same bond length of Ru-Ru scattering path is visualized, and one smaller peak at ≈1.59 Å is ascribed to Ru-O-Ni coordination.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ FT-IR during OER shows intensified HOO* peaks at ≈1100 cm^{-1} and NiOOH characteristic peaks at 1632 and 3074 cm^{-1}.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ FT-IR during the OER process was operated at the open circuit potential and potential range between 1.2 and 1.8 V (vs RHE). The infrared vibration peaks at ≈1100 cm^{-1} became stronger and stronger with the increasing voltage...

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern confirms generation of Ru NPs on amorphous Ni(OH)2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction pattern (Figure S3, Supporting Information) and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) image (Figure 1i) confirmed the generation of Ru NPs on the amorphous Ni(OH)2 (Ru - N_i(OH)_2).
